visual_evidence: A light-colored cylindrical wooden dowel lies diagonally across a wooden workbench and is broken into two pieces in the lower-middle of the frame.
A long, sharp splinter protrudes downward along the longitudinal grain from the left side of the upper broken end.
The matching left side of the lower piece shows an elongated groove along the grain where the splinter pulled out.
The opposite (right) side of both broken ends shows a stepped, slightly jagged fracture running across the grain.
No knots, holes, notches, or dark rot discolouration are visible at the break; the wood grain runs nearly parallel to the dowel axis.
diagnosis.probable_cause: A single bending load exceeded the flexural strength of the dowel. Tension on one side pulled out a long splinter along the grain while the opposite compression side broke across the grain in a stepped fracture, typical of sound wood overloaded in bending.
alternative_modes: A brash (brittle) wood failure from decay or severe cross-grain defect would produce an abrupt, flat break across the grain with very short or no splinters, whereas this fracture has a long splinter along straight grain. Metal and FDM modes do not apply because the part is clearly solid wood.

solutions.title: Shorten the unsupported span or add a central support
solutions.description: Move the supports closer together or place an intermediate support near the point of load application to reduce the peak bending moment on the dowel.
pros: Directly reduces the bending stress without changing the dowel diameter
Keeps existing mating holes and hardware unchanged
cons: Requires adding or relocating a support feature in the assembly
May obstruct clearance along the span

solutions.title: Reposition the applied load closer to a support
solutions.description: Shift the point where force is applied toward the supported ends rather than mid-span, lowering the lever arm creating the bending moment.
pros: Lowers peak bending moment proportionally to the reduced lever arm
Requires no extra material or heavier dowel
cons: Changes load geometry and may require modifying mating parts

solutions.title: Increase the dowel diameter or use a deeper section
solutions.description: Replace the dowel with a larger-diameter rod or orient a rectangular section with greater depth in the bending direction.
pros: Bending strength increases rapidly with section depth (cubed for a circular diameter)
cons: Requires enlarging mating holes or brackets

solutions.title: Switch to a higher-strength straight-grained hardwood or composite rod
solutions.description: Use a tougher, higher-modulus species such as hickory or ash with verified straight grain, or substitute a fiberglass or metal rod if geometry cannot change.
pros: Drop-in replacement with identical outer dimensions
No changes needed to mating holes or supports
cons: Higher material cost and potentially longer sourcing time
Does not reduce the applied bending moment
